elements.element: No exclusivity or 'sole supplier' obligation binding Customer
elements.evidence: 12.3 'Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.'

elements.element: No de facto sourcing restraint (disclose-and-match / right of first refusal) before Customer engages another provider
elements.evidence: 7.2 as redlined: 'Customer need not disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.'

elements.element: Customer free to engage any supplier and conduct business in any field or territory
elements.evidence: 12.3 'Nothing restricts Customer from ... engaging any supplier, ... or conducting business in any field or territory.'

elements.element: Any exclusivity limited to a defined product category
elements.evidence: Condition absent — no exclusivity of any scope is imposed: 'Customer has made no exclusivity ... commitment.'
Condition absent — no exclusivity term exists to limit; 7.2 restraint removed by 'need not disclose or match'.

elements.element: Automatic termination of exclusivity on Vendor's service-level or delivery-date failure
elements.evidence: Condition absent — no exclusivity obligation remains that would require an exit trigger.

reasons: The single operator flip in 7.2 ('must disclose and match' → 'need not disclose or match') removes the de facto right of first refusal, so no exclusivity or sole-supplier restraint binds Customer; the preferred position is fully met.
Section 12.3's affirmative non-exclusivity confirmation is untouched and now consistent with 7.2, eliminating the prior contradiction.

Edit is confined to the offending phrase inside one sentence — no new exceptions, no boilerplate, no whole-clause rewrite; the fallback construct suggested in the comment was correctly kept non-operative.
Fallback elements are satisfied vacuously because no exclusivity obligation of any scope or duration survives; no preferred/fallback mixing occurred.
All unrelated terms remain effective and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
